comparisonWithQwen.note: Qwen's own context-ablation cohort (eval/a99-closed-loop/direct-semantic-context-ablation-score-v1, rescored under R2 in gold-r2-rescore/) shows the mirror-image pattern.

qwen.F1: correct (DOCUMENT_LABEL) in all three arms, including FULL_CONTEXT
qwen.Agenda: wrong (DOCUMENT_LABEL instead of STRUCTURAL_UNIT) under FULL_CONTEXT and LOCAL_CONTEXT_RADIUS_3; correct only under MINIMAL_STRUCTURAL_CONTEXT_V1

haiku.F1: wrong (never DOCUMENT_LABEL) under FULL_CONTEXT and LOCAL_CONTEXT_RADIUS_3; correct only under MINIMAL_STRUCTURAL_CONTEXT_V1
haiku.Agenda: correct (STRUCTURAL_UNIT) in all three arms, including FULL_CONTEXT

comparisonWithQwen.interpretation: Both models perform best under MINIMAL_STRUCTURAL_CONTEXT_V1 (18/18 and, for Qwen, its own 18/18 under R2), so narrower context is genuinely helpful on this document. But the two models are not sensitive to context in the same place: narrowing context fixes Qwen's Agenda confusion while leaving F1 unaffected (F1 is already correct for Qwen in every arm under R2); narrowing context fixes Haiku's F1 confusion while leaving Agenda unaffected (Agenda is already correct for Haiku in every arm). Neither model shows the other model's context-sensitive failure. This weakens any claim that MINIMAL_STRUCTURAL_CONTEXT_V1 helps for a single shared mechanistic reason across models - each model's own confusion is narrowed differently by the same context reduction.
